Body: We should also wire the utility-process crash/error path, not just a plain `exit` callback. VS Code registers stdout, stderr, message, spawn, exit, and `app.child-process-gone` filtered by service name so it can distinguish clean exit from crash/oom/launch-failed and clear process state. At minimum add `child.on('error')` and `app.on('child-process-gone')` filtering `serviceName: 'opencode server'` so sidecar failures are visible in logs.

Suggestion for the human to decide: now that this dialog is driven by any retry action, this Go-specific dismissal flag can suppress unrelated actions. For example, choosing dont show again on the PAYG prompt would also hide the free-limit Go upsell later, and an existing Go upsell dismissal would hide PAYG. Consider keying the throttle/dismissal state by action type or link instead of sharing GO_UPSELL_DONT_SHOW/GO_UPSELL_LAST_SEEN_AT for every action.

`collect()` uses `statSync()` (follows symlinks) and then reads the resolved path into the zip. If a log directory contains a symlink (or is replaced with one), exporting logs could inadvertently include arbitrary files outside the intended log roots. Consider using `lstatSync()` to detect and skip symlinks, and/or enforcing that `realpath` stays within the expected base directory before adding to the archive.

`stamp()` drops milliseconds, so it has only second-level resolution. That can cause run directory name collisions (two app launches within the same second) and export zip filename collisions (multiple exports in the same second), mixing logs or overwriting the previous archive. Include milliseconds or add a random suffix/counter to guarantee uniqueness.

The exported `manifest()` includes absolute paths (`userData`, `logs`, `crashDumps`) and other potentially sensitive environment details. Since the archive is intended to be shared for debugging, consider redacting user-identifying path components (e.g., username/home dir) and/or showing a user-facing warning about what information will be included.

`writeZip()` reads every file fully into memory and then materializes the entire zip as an ArrayBuffer before writing. With many log files (even if each is capped), this can cause high peak memory usage during export. Consider streaming entries to disk (or enforcing a total export size limit) to keep memory bounded.

The `responsive` handler logs at error level (`log.error` / `writeLog`), which will create noisy error logs for a successful recovery scenario. This looks more appropriate as `info` (or `warn` if you want to highlight a prior unresponsive episode).

The new command title is hard-coded as "Export logs" while surrounding command titles are localized via `language.t(...)`. To keep the command palette consistent and translatable, add an i18n key and use `language.t(...)` here as well.

`decodeURIComponent(url.pathname)` can throw (e.g., malformed percent-encoding). Since this runs inside the protocol handler, an invalid/malicious URL could cause the handler to reject/throw rather than cleanly returning 404. Consider wrapping the decode in a try/catch and treating decode errors as "Not found" (and optionally logging at a low level to avoid log spam).

The animation teardown uses a hard-coded 600ms timeout, but the actual transition durations are configurable via CSS vars (e.g. --tool-motion-spring-ms / --tool-motion-fade-ms in tool-status-title.css). If those vars are increased, `finish()` will run early and unmount one of the labels mid-transition. Consider using a `transitionend` listener on `widthRef` (and/or computing the timeout from computed styles / CSS vars) instead of a fixed 600ms.

`finish()` calls `cancelAnimationFrame(frame)` unconditionally. Elsewhere in this package (e.g. text-reveal.tsx) there are guards for environments where RAF/cancelRAF may be missing. Consider adding `typeof cancelAnimationFrame === "function"` (and similarly guarding RAF usage) to avoid runtime errors in non-browser/test environments.

Because the rendered text updates directly from `activeTail`/`doneTail`, if only the label text changes (e.g. i18n update) while `props.active` stays the same, the DOM will already be at the new width by the time this effect runs. In that case `first = contentWidth(widthRef)` measures the new width and you lose the intended width-slide from the previous label. If you want slide-on-text-change too, consider storing the displayed label strings in state and only updating them after capturing the previous width.

In this manager, `key` is `directoryKey(directory)` (a normalized path). Passing `key` into `input.queryOptions.*` means the query option factory may create/select an SDK client using the normalized string rather than the original `directory` value. That changes the directory value sent to the server and can make behavior depend on call order (first caller determines what gets cached under the same `directoryKey`), which is especially risky on Windows/UNC paths and with trailing-slash differences. Prefer calling the query option factories with the original `directory` string and have the factories normalize only the `queryKey` (or accept both `directory` and `key` explicitly).

`createChildStoreManager` now types `queryOptions` using `ReturnType<typeof load*Query>`, which forces value imports of those `load*Query` functions even if they’re only used for typing. Because this module and `../global-sync` import each other, this can keep/strengthen a runtime circular dependency unnecessarily. Consider exporting explicit type aliases for the query option shapes (or using TanStack Query’s `QueryOptions`/`CreateQueryOptions` types) so this can be a type-only dependency.

This event-driven LSP refresh passes `key` (a `directoryKey`-normalized path) into `queryOptionsApi.lsp()`, which then calls `sdkFor(directory)`. That can cause the SDK client to be created/selected using the normalized key rather than the actual directory string from the event, and makes the cached client’s `directory` value depend on which codepath runs first. Prefer using `directory` here (and, if desired, normalize only the queryKey inside the query option factory).

PR description mentions routing key-only consumers through `queryOptions.keys`, but the new API exposed here is `queryOptions.<resource>(...).queryKey` (no `keys` namespace). Either update the PR description to match the implemented API or add the `keys` helper object if that was the intended public surface.

Suggestion: consider registering the signal handlers before starting the child, with the handler re-raising if no child has been assigned yet. As written, a termination signal that lands after `spawn()` returns but before the `process.on(...)` calls can still terminate the wrapper without forwarding, leaving the same orphaned child this PR is trying to prevent.

Importing `Provider` from `@/provider/provider` pulls in the full provider implementation (large module with many deps) just to parse a `provider/model` string. This can unnecessarily increase tool load time / bundle size. Consider moving `parseModel` into a lightweight module (e.g. `src/provider/schema.ts` or a small `util/model.ts`) and importing from there, or otherwise avoiding the heavy provider module here.

`params.model` is accepted as an arbitrary string, but `Provider.parseModel()` just splits on "/" and does not validate that both `providerID` and `modelID` are non-empty. Passing an invalid value like "gpt-4o" or "openai/" would silently produce an empty provider/model and likely fail later in a harder-to-debug way. Add explicit validation here (and/or in the parameter schema) and fail early with a clear error message when the format is not `provider/model`.

Suggestion: sorting by byte size picks the smallest successful candidate, which will usually choose the most compressed JPEG even when a higher-quality JPEG at the same dimensions is still under the limit. Consider preserving the preference order among candidates that fit, or otherwise selecting the highest-quality acceptable output rather than the smallest one.

Suggestion: if auto_resize is false, this returns the image before checking max_width, max_height, or max_base64_bytes, so disabling resizing also disables the advertised max-size guard. If the intended behavior is to reject instead of resize when resizing is disabled, consider doing the decode/limit check before this branch and only skipping the resize attempts.

Suggestion: this manual in-flight Promise cache appears to violate the local Effect guidance to use Effect.cached for deduplication instead of storing Promise | undefined state. Consider moving Photon loading into the layer as a cached Effect so concurrent callers still share the import without module-level mutable promise state.

Suggestion: since prompt now exposes Image.Error as an expected failure, consider mapping it in the HTTP prompt endpoint as well. That handler wraps promptSvc.prompt in Stream.fromEffect, so an invalid or oversize user image can fail while streaming the response body instead of returning the declared BadRequest contract.

Suggestion: because normalization happens inside completeToolCall, the earlier EventV2 Tool.Success event still publishes value.output.attachments before images are resized or omitted. EventV2 consumers can therefore receive an oversized image even though the persisted tool part is fixed; consider normalizing before building that event or returning the normalized attachments for the event.

Suggestion: this config schema change likely needs the generated JS SDK/OpenAPI artifacts regenerated. packages/sdk/js/src/v2/gen/types.gen.ts still has Config without attachment, so SDK consumers will not see the new option even though runtime config accepts it. The repo instructions call out ./packages/sdk/js/script/build.ts for schema changes.

Suggestion: consider leaving Image.Service as an explicit dependency and providing Image.layer once at the default/app layer boundary instead of inside SessionPrompt.layer. This is also done in SessionProcessor.layer, so the app can instantiate multiple Image services/caches; because Image.layer temporarily monkey-patches global fs.readFileSync while importing photon, duplicate concurrent initialization can race and leave the global patch installed. Keeping the dependency explicit matches the Effect layer guidance and avoids duplicate importer state.

Suggestion, human can decide: this type alias appears to be unused. Since the style guide asks us to avoid extra single-use or unnecessary names, consider removing it unless it is intended for a near-term exported API.

Suggestion, human can decide: `chat.message` now receives `resolvedParts`, but the saved message and Prompted event use the normalized `parts` built just below. That means plugins can observe or mutate the pre-resize image data, including large base64 payloads that are not what the model ultimately receives. Consider normalizing before this hook, or otherwise make the hook payload match the persisted parts.

Suggestion, human can decide: the wasm file import happens before the try/catch, so if the bundled wasm asset is missing or fails to resolve, normalize can fail with that raw import defect instead of the typed PhotonUnavailableError exposed by Image.normalize. Consider moving this import inside the try so all Photon loading failures follow the same error path.

Suggestion for human discretion: this normalizes only the current prompt parts before they are saved, so an oversized image that is already stored in session history can still be replayed unchanged on the next model call. That leaves the unrecoverable-history case from #23570 in place for existing sessions or any bypassed path; consider adding a replay-time safeguard in MessageV2.toModelMessagesEffect to normalize or omit oversized media before sending it to the provider.

Suggestion for human to decide: this checks all configured git references, but refs with the same cache path and a different branch are intentionally skipped from `materializeByPath` above. With two refs to the same repo on different branches, the skipped ref can still bypass `external_directory` and its generated agent points at a cache populated for another branch. Consider deriving containment/agent usability from the materialized refs only, or marking conflicting refs invalid.

The `CodeRenderable` integration test still passes `onChunks: detectLinks` directly, so it won’t fail if the production wiring (`onChunks={detectLinks}` in `routes/session/index.tsx`) is removed/regresses. `File.read()` runs in the server (including the Node adapter used by Desktop), but this new sampling logic calls `Bun.file(...)` unguarded. In non-Bun runtimes this will throw at runtime and break file preview. Replace this with a runtime-agnostic partial read (e.g., `node:fs/promises` open+read of the first N bytes, or add a small helper on AppFileSystem for reading a prefix) instead of relying on the Bun global.

This adds coverage for an extensionless binary, but the new sampling logic also changes behavior for extensionless *text* files (now they get scanned before `readFileString`). Consider adding a test for an extensionless UTF-8 text file to ensure it still returns `{ type: "text" }` and isn’t misclassified by the heuristic.

`detectLinks` is now wired into the main session renderer’s markdown `<code>` path, but there are other TUI code paths that still render `filetype="markdown"` without `onChunks={detectLinks}` (e.g. `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/feature-plugins/system/session-v2.tsx` around the `AssistantText` / `AssistantReasoning` markdown `<code>` renderables). If that view is enabled (it’s gated behind `Flag.OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_EVENT_SYSTEM`), long wrapped URLs may still be unclickable there. Consider wiring `detectLinks` into those `<code filetype="markdown">` usages as well, or explicitly scoping/annotating why this fix intentionally only applies to `routes/session`.

2. `AssistantText` (line 372)  
3. `AssistantReasoning` (line 401)

`flushDeferredMounts()` sets `deferredFrame` to `undefined` before shifting/invoking the next mount. If a deferred mount schedules another deferred mount synchronously (e.g., via nested components mounting during the callback), `scheduleDeferredFlush()` can observe `deferredFrame === undefined` and schedule an additional RAF chain while the current flush is still in progress. This can lead to multiple concurrent flush loops and more than one deferred mount being executed per frame (and `deferredFrame` being overwritten, making cancellation/implied single-flight behavior unreliable). Consider keeping a separate `flushing`/`scheduled` flag (or using a sentinel value) so `scheduleDeferredFlush()` cannot schedule while a flush is active, and only one RAF chain can be in flight at a time.

Suggestion only: this prompt file was ASCII before, but the new text introduces non-ASCII punctuation such as em dashes/arrows. The repo style asks us to default to ASCII unless there is a clear justification, so consider using plain "-" / "->" punctuation for consistency. The human reviewer can decide whether this matters for prompt readability.

`lowerUserPart` converts every `MediaPart` into an OpenAI `image_url` block without validating `mediaType`. If a caller attaches a non-image (e.g. `application/pdf`), this will still be sent as `image_url` and is expected to be rejected by OpenAI-compatible backends. Consider explicitly rejecting non-`image/*` media types here (or add support for other OpenAI content block types if intended).

`contentBlocks` is built from `message.content` using a forced cast (`as TextPart | MediaPart`). Although the earlier loop returns early on unsupported parts, this cast bypasses type safety and can hide future regressions if new part types are added. Consider collecting validated parts in the loop (narrowed to text/media) and mapping that array instead, so no cast is needed.

Tests cover image media lowering, but there is no coverage for rejecting/handling non-image `MediaPart` (e.g. `application/pdf` or `audio/*`). Since Chat Completions `image_url` blocks are image-only, add a test asserting that non-image media is rejected (or handled via the appropriate OpenAI content block type if you intend to support it).

Suggestion only: this condensed rule now allows force-push when explicitly requested, but the old prompt had a stricter guard to never force-push main/master and warn the user instead. It seems worth preserving that default-branch safety check in compact form so an assistant does not comply with a destructive force-push to the primary branch. The human reviewer can decide whether that tradeoff is acceptable.

Suggestion for the author to decide: this mouse path can still mutate the prompt while `props.disabled` is true. The rest of this component blocks typing, paste, and submit while disabled, so `onMouseUp` should probably return before calling `expandPasteBlockAtMouse(event)` to avoid editing a disabled prompt during permission/question prompts.

Suggestion (style): this new metadata type uses `any`, which the repo style guide asks us to avoid. Since this is client-controlled JSON and the generated SDK exposes `unknown`, consider carrying `Record<string, unknown>` through the storage/service types instead of `Record<string, any>`.

Suggestion: the update route accepts `metadata: null` to clear metadata, but the generated SDK type only allows an object here. That means SDK callers cannot type-safely use the clear path covered by the API/tests. Since this file is generated, the source fix may need to make the nullable schema survive generation so this becomes `{ [key: string]: unknown } | null`.

`<use href={...}>` relies on the sprite being present in the initial HTML. Right now the sprite is only injected via `onMount(ensureSprite)`, which does not run during SSR and only runs after hydration/mount, so SSR pages that render icons (e.g. SolidStart routes) will show missing icons until JS hydrates (and never show them if hydration is disabled/fails). Consider rendering the sprite as part of the document markup (e.g. an `IconSprite` component included once near the root/document body) so symbols exist at first paint, while keeping `<use>` for client-side performance.

`onMount(ensureSprite)` runs for every `Icon` instance; even though `ensureSprite` bails out after insertion, each mount still does a `document.getElementById` lookup. If many icons mount in a tight window (your benchmark scenario), this per-instance DOM query can add avoidable overhead; consider guarding with a module-level boolean (or similar) so subsequent icons skip the DOM query entirely after the first successful injection.

`fetchOlderMessages` sets `shift` to true before awaiting `loadMore()`, but if `loadMore()` throws/rejects (network error) or the function returns early due to session change, `shift` may never be reset to false. This can leave the timeline Virtualizer in perpetual shift mode and cause incorrect scroll compensation. Wrap the body in a try/finally (or ensure every return path clears `shift`) so shift is always reset after the fetch attempt completes/fails.

`assistantCopyPartID(...)` and `turnDurationMs(...)` are recomputed by scanning all assistant messages/parts every time an assistant-part row renders. On turns with many parts/groups this becomes quadratic and can offset the virtualization gains. Consider computing these once per `userMessageID` (e.g., in `messageRowMemos` or a memoized map keyed by `userMessageID`) and reusing the cached values when rendering each row.

Suggestion: `Flag.OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` is captured at module load, while this loader later reads `process.env.OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` dynamically. If a test or embedder sets `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` after import, this guard still creates the global stub even though config was explicitly routed through content. Suggestion: this check only considers `config.json`, `opencode.json`, and `opencode.jsonc`, so a user who still has the legacy global `config` file will get a new `opencode.jsonc` stub before the legacy migration runs. `vcsDir` is now the realpath of the git dir. That means a user config that previously ignored the symlink path returned by `path.resolve(ctx.worktree, --git-dir)` (e.g. `/project/.git`) will no longer match `cfgIgnores.includes(vcsDir)`, and the watcher will subscribe anyway. Consider checking both the pre-realpath value (`resolved`) and the post-realpath value (`vcsDir`), or normalizing `cfgIgnores` to handle both paths consistently.

The new symlink-handling branch (`realpath` + fallback) isn’t covered by existing watcher tests. Adding a regression test that creates a worktree with a symlinked `.git` and asserts the watcher still publishes `.git/HEAD` updates would help prevent future regressions (especially for the repo-tool layout described in #26981).

`createScopedAttention().soundboard.registerPack()` assumes every `pack.sounds` value is a string and calls `resolvePluginFile(root, file)` unconditionally. At runtime a plugin can pass `undefined`/non-string values (even though the TS type is `Partial<Record<..., string>>`), which will throw on `file.startsWith(...)` and can crash plugin initialization. Filter entries to `typeof file === "string" && file.trim().length > 0` (and ideally only allow known sound-name keys) before resolving, or make `resolvePluginFile` accept `unknown` and safely ignore invalid values.

Suggestion for the human reviewer to consider: the empty tree hash is still a useful baseline. Returning undefined here means an empty repo has no initial snapshot, so if the first assistant response creates files there is no baseline to diff/revert against and the response will not get a patch/undo entry. Keeping the empty tree hash should preserve tracking of first-file additions while still failing closed on real git failures.

This file is implemented as a standalone script (manual assert counters + console logs) rather than a Bun test suite. When run under `bun test`, it will likely report 0 tests and `process.exit(1)` can terminate the whole test runner abruptly on failure. Please rewrite this using `describe/test/expect` from `bun:test` (and ideally `testEffect` + scoped temp dirs) so failures are reported normally and cleanup is guaranteed.

ID generation (`Date.now()` + per-process counter) can collide across multiple OpenCode sessions/processes (the main use case for Teams). Two processes creating tasks/messages in the same millisecond can overwrite the same `{id}.json` file. Use a cross-process unique ID (e.g. `crypto.randomUUID()` or include pid + randomness) to avoid collisions.

`claimTask` has a TOCTOU race: two sessions can both read `pending` and then both write `claimed`, resulting in double-claims in real multi-process usage. This needs an atomic claim mechanism (e.g. use `EffectFlock`/lock directory keyed by task file, or an atomic exclusive-create/rename workflow) so only one claimant can succeed.

`completeTask` does not verify who claimed the task (there’s no `sessionID` in input, and no check against `task.assignee`). That allows any session with the team_id/task_id to complete someone else’s work. Consider requiring `sessionID` and enforcing `task.assignee === sessionID` (or limiting completion to the lead) to preserve task integrity.
